# sitegen

Builds `content/` into a small browsable site under `out/`: an index listing the
posts, an about page, and one page per post, sharing navigation and a stylesheet.

    python3 build.py

Content is Markdown with a `---` front-matter header (`title`, `date`). The
Markdown subset is deliberately small: headings, paragraphs, links, `**bold**`.

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

## Writing posts

Add a file to `content/posts/` with a `.md` extension. It needs a front-matter
header with at least a `title` and `date`:

    ---
    title: My post title
    date: 2026-09-18
    ---

    # My post title

    Your body text here. Supports headings (`#`, `##`, `###`), paragraphs,
    links (`[text](url)`), and `**bold**`.

Then run `python3 build.py` to regenerate the site. The new post will appear on
the index automatically, sorted by date (newest first).

## Project layout

- `content/posts/` -- blog posts (Markdown)
- `content/index.md` -- homepage content (appears above the post list)
- `content/about.md` -- about page
- `templates/page.html` -- shared HTML template
- `static/style.css` -- shared stylesheet
- `build.py` -- the build script (no dependencies beyond Python stdlib)
- `tests/` -- unit tests

## Serving locally

    cd out && python3 -m http.server 8000

Then open http://localhost:8000/ in a browser.

name: sitegen
description: Use when building or debugging the sitegen static site generator. Content-to-HTML pipeline with link verification.
category: software-development

# sitegen

Static site generator for a small blog. Builds `content/` Markdown into `out/` HTML.

## Layout

- `content/posts/*.md` -- blog posts (front-matter: title, date)
- `content/index.md`, `content/about.md` -- top-level pages
- `templates/page.html` -- shared template with `{{title}}`, `{{nav}}`, `{{stylesheet}}`, `{{content}}` placeholders
- `static/style.css` -- shared stylesheet
- `build.py` -- build script (stdlib only)
- `tests/test_build.py` -- unit tests

## Build & test

    python3 build.py
    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

## Key behavior

- Posts go to `out/posts/<slug>.html`; top-level pages to `out/<slug>.html`
- Nav and stylesheet links use relative prefixes (posts use `../`)
- Index lists all posts sorted by date (newest first)
- Markdown subset: headings (#, ##, ###), paragraphs, links, **bold**

## Verifying links

    from pathlib import Path
    from html.parser import HTMLParser
    # Parse each HTML file in out/, extract hrefs from <a> and <link> tags,
    # resolve relative to the file's parent, assert all targets exist.

## Adding a post

1. Create `content/posts/my-post.md` with front-matter header
2. Run `python3 build.py`
3. Link appears on index automatically

Done. The site was almost ready but had a real bug: post pages in `out/posts/` had nav and stylesheet links pointing to `index.html` and `style.css` relative to their own directory, so clicking Home or About from any post led to a 404. Fixed by making the template use relative prefixes (`../`) for posts, added a regression test, and rewrote the README with instructions for the colleague.

Verified: 6/6 unit tests pass, all links across all 5 HTML pages resolve, and the output tree is clean (index, about, 3 posts, stylesheet). Ready to hand off.
